questions.question: What does Ganesha love to do with Mr. Mouse? How do they have fun together?
questions.explanation: Helps children connect with the characters and see how they are curious and enjoy exploring together, setting up why the story matters to them.

questions.question: Why shouldn’t Ganesha eat the super jumbo jawbreaker laddoo? What happened when he tried?
questions.explanation: Makes sure children understand Ganesha’s mistake and the unexpected thing that happened, a key part of the moral lesson.

questions.question: How did Ganesha feel when his tusk broke? Have you ever felt worried about how you look?
questions.explanation: Encourages children to relate to Ganesha’s feelings about looking different and start to reflect on accepting themselves.

questions.question: What do Ganesha and Mr. Mouse do when they try to fix the tusk? How do you feel when you try to fix a problem and it doesn’t work right away?
questions.explanation: Helps children recognize frustration and perseverance, linking to using what makes you special even when things seem hard.

questions.question: What did Ganesha do with his broken tusk that made him feel happy again?
questions.explanation: Connects the turning point in the story to the moral—Ganesha finds a new purpose with his difference.

questions.question: Can you think of something about you that is special, even if it’s different from your friends? How can you use it in a good way?
questions.explanation: Helps children relate the story’s message to their own lives, encouraging self-acceptance and thinking positively about differences.

questions.question: Why was Ganesha proud at the end of the story? What made him happy?
questions.explanation: Encourages children to see the value in Ganesha’s actions rather than his appearance, connecting to the lesson of helping others and feeling fulfilled.

questions.question: Have you ever helped a friend or done something important in your own special way, even if it was different from others?
questions.explanation: Encourages children to make personal connections and share how being different can help them do good things, linking real life to the story’s moral.

questions.question: If you see someone who looks or does things differently, how can you be a good friend to them?
questions.explanation: Promotes empathy and acceptance in everyday life, teaching that you can help and support others no matter what they look like.

moral: Even when something unexpected or bad happens, you can find new ways to use what makes you special and do important things. It’s okay to look different — you can still help others and be happy.
learning_objectives: Children will be able to describe what makes Ganesha special and how he uses his differences to do something important.
Children will be able to share times they felt different or faced a challenge and discuss how they felt.
Children will be able to think of ways to be kind and accepting of others who may look or act differently.
Children will be able to relate the story’s moral to their own experiences, understanding that everyone has special qualities to share.
